application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
decision_conditions: The Local Planning Authority raises no objection to the felling of the three Cypress trees (T2, T3 and T4) detailed within the Section 211 notification. However, the Council considers the proposed felling of the mature Sycamore tree (T1)  to be unacceptable due to its significant size, high public visibility, and contribution to the visual amenity of the Carshalton Village Conservation Area. Consequently, to prevent the avoidable loss of this key landscape feature, the Council has made Tree Preservation Order TPO 2026/03 to afford the Sycamore formal statutory protection.In making TPO 2026/03, full consideration was given to the submitted structural appraisal regarding the severe lean of the historic boundary wall and the observed root influence. While retaining the tree increases the technical complexity of rebuilding the wall, the structural report highlights that engineered foundation solutions—such as localised deepening, pile and ground beam arrangements, or bridging—remain available to facilitate reconstruction without removing the tree. The wholesale removal of a prominent amenity tree is considered a disproportionate response where alternative structural engineering options exist.Furthermore, a Section 211 notification does not provide the legal mechanism for the Council to secure replacement tree planting or attach enforceable conditions. The making of TPO 2026/03 ensures that the tree is preserved in the interest of public amenity, while establishing a formal statutory process to control any future arboricultural works or enforce compensatory planting should felling be demonstrated as unavoidable on structural grounds.
